items.sql: SELECT channel_cd, COUNT(*) FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts BETWEEN '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY channel_cd ORDER BY channel_cd

items.question: Find the total order amount for customers in the 'NA' region whose orders were placed between 2026-01-01 and 2026-06-30 in USD currency.
items.sql: SELECT SUM(t1.ord_total_amt) FROM ord_hdr AS t1 INNER JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t2.region_cd = 'NA' AND t1.currency_cd = 'USD' AND t1.ord_dt BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-06-30'

items.question: List customer names who have both a support ticket opened between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30 and an order placed in April 2026, ordered by customer name.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1.cust_nm FROM cust_master AS t1 INNER JOIN support_tkt AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS t3 ON t1.cust_id = t3.cust_id WHERE t2.opened_ts BETWEEN '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-04-30 23:59:59' AND t3.ord_dt BETWEEN '2026-04-01' AND '2026-04-30' ORDER BY t1.cust_nm ASC

items.question: Show the employee name and the count of ticket events where the event type was 'CLOSE' and happened between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30, for employees in the 'SUP' department.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_nm, COUNT(t2.evt_id) FROM emp AS t1 INNER JOIN tkt_event AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.actor_emp_id WHERE t1.dept_cd = 'SUP' AND t2.evt_type = 'CLOSE' AND t2.evt_ts BETWEEN '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm ORDER BY COUNT(t2.evt_id) DESC, t1.emp_id ASC

items.question: For each loyalty tier, calculate the average order total amount for orders placed between 2026-01-01 and 2026-07-31.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tier_cd, AVG(t2.ord_total_amt) FROM cust_master AS t1 INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t2.ord_dt BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' GROUP BY t1.tier_cd ORDER BY t1.tier_cd ASC

items.question: Find the maximum refund amount requested for orders placed through the 'WEB' channel where the request date was between 2025-11-01 and 2025-12-31.
items.sql: SELECT MAX(t1.rfd_amt) FROM refund_req AS t1 INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id WHERE t2.channel_cd = 'WEB' AND t1.req_dt BETWEEN '2025-11-01' AND '2025-12-31'

items.question: List the ticket id and customer name for critical severity support tickets (sev_lvl = 1) opened between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30 that remained unassigned (assigned_emp_id is null).
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t2.cust_nm FROM support_tkt AS t1 INNER JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.sev_lvl = 1 AND t1.assigned_emp_id IS NULL AND t1.opened_ts BETWEEN '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND '2026-04-30 23:59:59' ORDER BY t1.opened_ts ASC, t1.tkt_id ASC

items.question: Show the policy rule key and its value for rules that were in force on 2026-04-15.
items.sql: SELECT rule_key, rule_val FROM policy_rule WHERE eff_from <= '2026-04-15' AND (eff_to >= '2026-04-15' OR eff_to IS NULL)

items.question: For customers who signed up between 2022-01-01 and 2022-07-31, show their customer id, name, and the count of orders they placed between 2026-01-01 and 2026-07-31, ordered by order count descending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm, COUNT(t2.ord_id) FROM cust_master AS t1 LEFT JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id AND t2.ord_dt BETWEEN '2026-01-01' AND '2026-07-31' WHERE t1.signup_dt BETWEEN '2022-01-01' AND '2022-07-31' GROUP BY t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm ORDER BY COUNT(t2.ord_id) DESC, t1.cust_id ASC

items.question: Can you group all support tickets opened in 2026 by month and show the year-month along with the ticket count, in chronological order?
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND opened_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Please pull a quarterly breakdown of support ticket volumes for the year 2026, showing the quarter number and total tickets, ordered from Q1 to Q4.
items.sql: SELECT QUARTER(opened_ts) AS qtr, COUNT(*) AS tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND opened_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY QUARTER(opened_ts) ORDER BY qtr ASC;

items.question: What does our monthly refund request volume look like for all of 2025? Show the year-month and count of requests, sorted by month ascending.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(req_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS rfd_cnt FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(req_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Give me the quarterly count of refund requests submitted during 2026, ordered chronologically by quarter.
items.sql: SELECT QUARTER(req_dt) AS qtr, COUNT(*) AS rfd_cnt FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND req_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY QUARTER(req_dt) ORDER BY qtr ASC;

items.question: Show me the weekly count of new support tickets opened between 2026-04-01 and 2026-05-31, listing the year and week number with the count in time order.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%x-%v') AS yr_week, COUNT(*) AS tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts >= '2026-04-01' AND opened_ts < '2026-06-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%x-%v') ORDER BY yr_week ASC;

items.question: For orders placed in 2026, break down the total order amount by month. Show year-month and sum of ord_total_amt, sorted chronologically.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, SUM(ord_total_amt) AS total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: We need a quarterly trend of total order revenue for 2025 and 2026 combined. List the year, quarter, and total amount, ordered by year and quarter.
items.sql: SELECT YEAR(ord_dt) AS yr, QUARTER(ord_dt) AS qtr, SUM(ord_total_amt) AS total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND ord_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR(ord_dt), QUARTER(ord_dt) ORDER BY yr ASC, qtr ASC;

items.question: Can you summarize refund amounts requested each month throughout 2025? Display year-month and total requested amount, ordered by month.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(req_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, SUM(rfd_amt) AS total_rfd_amt FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt < '2026-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(req_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Show the monthly count of customer signups across the entire year 2022, sorted chronologically by year-month.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(signup_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS signup_cnt FROM cust_master WHERE signup_dt >= '2022-01-01' AND signup_dt < '2023-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(signup_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: How many customer signups did we get by quarter in 2022? Display quarter and count, ordered from Q1 to Q4.
items.sql: SELECT QUARTER(signup_dt) AS qtr, COUNT(*) AS signup_cnt FROM cust_master WHERE signup_dt >= '2022-01-01' AND signup_dt < '2023-01-01' GROUP BY QUARTER(signup_dt) ORDER BY qtr ASC;

items.question: For 2026, let's look at support ticket volume month by month, but filtered only for tickets where channel_cd is WEB. Show year-month and ticket count, ordered by month.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' AND opened_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND opened_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Provide a monthly aggregation of refund requests that had a reason code of DMG (damaged) during 2025 and 2026. Show year-month and request count, in time order.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(req_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS rfd_cnt FROM refund_req WHERE reason_cd = 'DMG' AND req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(req_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Track the employee hiring timeline by year and quarter from 2018 through 2021. Show year, quarter, and number of hires, ordered chronologically.
items.sql: SELECT YEAR(hire_dt) AS yr, QUARTER(hire_dt) AS qtr, COUNT(*) AS hire_cnt FROM emp WHERE hire_dt >= '2018-01-01' AND hire_dt < '2022-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR(hire_dt), QUARTER(hire_dt) ORDER BY yr ASC, qtr ASC;

items.question: Show me the weekly count of orders placed in July 2026. List the year-week format and order count, sorted by week ascending.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%x-%v') AS yr_week, COUNT(*) AS ord_cnt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-07-01' AND ord_dt < '2026-08-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%x-%v') ORDER BY yr_week ASC;

items.question: Calculate the average order total amount for each month in 2026. Display year-month and average order amount, ordered by month.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, AVG(ord_total_amt) AS avg_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: What is the monthly count of support tickets that were closed during 2026? Group by year-month of closed_ts and show count, sorted chronologically.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(closed_ts, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS closed_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE closed_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND closed_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(closed_ts, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Break down the total refund amount decided each month in 2026 for requests where status_cd is A (approved). Show year-month and sum of refund amount, in chronological order.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(decided_ts, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, SUM(rfd_amt) AS total_approved_amt FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'A' AND decided_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND decided_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(decided_ts, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Let's review order volume by sales channel across months in Q1 and Q2 of 2026. Show year-month, channel_cd, and order count, sorted by month then channel.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, channel_cd, COUNT(*) AS ord_cnt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt < '2026-07-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m'), channel_cd ORDER BY month_str ASC, channel_cd ASC;

items.question: For tickets opened in April 2026, provide a weekly breakdown showing the year-week and count of tickets for each severity level (sev_lvl). Order by week ascending then severity level.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%x-%v') AS yr_week, sev_lvl, COUNT(*) AS tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts >= '2026-04-01' AND opened_ts < '2026-05-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%x-%v'), sev_lvl ORDER BY yr_week ASC, sev_lvl ASC;

items.question: Show the monthly count of ticket events of type 'CLOSE' recorded in tkt_event during 2026. List year-month and event count, ordered chronologically.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(evt_ts, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS evt_cnt FROM tkt_event WHERE evt_type = 'CLOSE' AND evt_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND evt_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(evt_ts, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: Give me a quarterly summary of unique customers who placed orders in 2026. Show year, quarter, and count of distinct customer IDs, ordered by year and quarter.
items.sql: SELECT YEAR(ord_dt) AS yr, QUARTER(ord_dt) AS qtr, COUNT(DISTINCT cust_id) AS distinct_cust_cnt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY YEAR(ord_dt), QUARTER(ord_dt) ORDER BY yr ASC, qtr ASC;

items.question: What are the monthly totals for order counts where the order status was C (cancelled) throughout 2026? Show year-month and count, sorted by month.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS cancelled_cnt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_status = 'C' AND ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(ord_dt, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: For all refund requests requested in 2026, group them by quarter and status code, showing the quarter, status_cd, and total refund amount. Order by quarter then status code.
items.sql: SELECT QUARTER(req_dt) AS qtr, status_cd, SUM(rfd_amt) AS total_rfd FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND req_dt < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY QUARTER(req_dt), status_cd ORDER BY qtr ASC, status_cd ASC;

items.question: Show the monthly count of support tickets categorized under category code 'TECH' for the year 2026. Display year-month and ticket count, in chronological order.
items.sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%Y-%m') AS month_str, COUNT(*) AS tkt_cnt FROM support_tkt WHERE categ_cd = 'TECH' AND opened_ts >= '2026-01-01' AND opened_ts < '2027-01-01' GROUP BY DATE_FORMAT(opened_ts, '%Y-%m') ORDER BY month_str ASC;

items.question: How many pending refund requests are there currently?
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'P';

items.question: List the full name and hire date of employees in the support department (SUP).
items.sql: SELECT emp_nm, hire_dt FROM emp WHERE dept_cd = 'SUP' ORDER BY hire_dt ASC, emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the support ticket ID and customer ID for tickets with critical severity (1).
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE sev_lvl = 1 ORDER BY opened_ts ASC, tkt_id ASC;

items.question: Count the number of active customers in the North America (NA) sales region.
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cust_master WHERE region_cd = 'NA' AND is_actv = 1;

items.question: Display the refund request ID and requested amount for requests due to damaged goods (DMG).
items.sql: SELECT rfd_id, rfd_amt FROM refund_req WHERE reason_cd = 'DMG' ORDER BY req_dt ASC, rfd_id ASC;

items.question: How many support tickets were opened through the mobile application (APP) channel?
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM support_tkt WHERE channel_cd = 'APP';

items.question: Show the customer ID and order total amount for orders placed via the web channel (WEB) on 2026-04-04.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id, ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' AND ord_dt = '2026-04-04' ORDER BY ord_id ASC;

items.question: Find the total requested refund amount for each refund reason code, sorted by total amount descending.
items.sql: SELECT reason_cd, SUM(rfd_amt) FROM refund_req GROUP BY reason_cd ORDER BY SUM(rfd_amt) DESC, reason_cd ASC;

items.question: List the full name of employees who have approved at least one refund request.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN refund_req r ON e.emp_id = r.approver_emp_id ORDER BY e.emp_nm ASC;

items.question: Show the order status and the count of orders for each status for orders placed since 2026-01-01.
items.sql: SELECT ord_status, COUNT(*) FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY ord_status ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, ord_status ASC;

items.question: What is the average requested refund amount for each refund status code?
items.sql: SELECT status_cd, AVG(rfd_amt) FROM refund_req GROUP BY status_cd ORDER BY status_cd ASC;

items.question: List the customer name and loyalty tier code for customers who signed up in July 2022.
items.sql: SELECT cust_nm, tier_cd FROM cust_master WHERE signup_dt >= '2022-07-01' AND signup_dt <= '2022-07-31' ORDER BY signup_dt ASC, cust_id ASC;

items.question: Find the employees who manage more than one direct report, showing their employee ID and the count of subordinates.
items.sql: SELECT mgr_emp_id, COUNT(*) FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY mgr_emp_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, mgr_emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the customer ID and total order amount for customers whose total order spending exceeds 1000 USD on orders placed in 2026.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id, SUM(ord_total_amt) FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND currency_cd = 'USD' GROUP BY cust_id HAVING SUM(ord_total_amt) > 1000.00 ORDER BY SUM(ord_total_amt) DESC, cust_id ASC;

items.question: Calculate the percentage of refund requests that have been approved out of all decided refund requests (ignoring pending ones).
items.sql: SELECT (SUM(CASE WHEN status_cd = 'A' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(*) FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd IN ('A', 'D');

items.question: List the customer ID and customer name for platinum tier (P) customers who have placed at least 1 order.
items.sql: SELECT c.cust_id, c.cust_nm FROM cust_master c JOIN ord_hdr o ON c.cust_id = o.cust_id WHERE c.tier_cd = 'P' GROUP BY c.cust_id, c.cust_nm HAVING COUNT(o.ord_id) >= 1 ORDER BY c.cust_id ASC;

items.question: For each support ticket category, find the maximum ticket severity level recorded.
items.sql: SELECT categ_cd, MIN(sev_lvl) FROM support_tkt GROUP BY categ_cd ORDER BY categ_cd ASC;

items.question: Show the employee ID and name of employees who have never been assigned any support tickets.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT assigned_emp_id FROM support_tkt WHERE assigned_emp_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Find the support ticket ID and the number of history events recorded for each ticket, keeping only tickets with more than 1 event.
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, COUNT(*) FROM tkt_event GROUP BY tkt_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, tkt_id ASC;

items.question: Show the department code and the total number of employees in each department.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, COUNT(*) FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, dept_cd ASC;

items.question: List the distinct order IDs that have more than one refund request associated with them.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id FROM refund_req GROUP BY ord_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY ord_id ASC;

items.question: What is the total refund amount requested per customer, considering only approved refunds?
items.sql: SELECT o.cust_id, SUM(r.rfd_amt) FROM refund_req r JOIN ord_hdr o ON r.ord_id = o.ord_id WHERE r.status_cd = 'A' GROUP BY o.cust_id ORDER BY SUM(r.rfd_amt) DESC, o.cust_id ASC;

items.question: Show the channel code and count of support tickets for each channel where the ticket was opened in April 2026.
items.sql: SELECT channel_cd, COUNT(*) FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY channel_cd ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, channel_cd ASC;

items.question: Find the employee ID and full name of employees who were hired before 2020.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE hire_dt < '2020-01-01' ORDER BY hire_dt ASC, emp_id ASC;

items.question: Which customer IDs placed an order through the web channel ('WEB') but never submitted a refund request? Return just the customer ID, ordered alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT c.cust_id FROM ord_hdr h JOIN refund_req r ON h.ord_id = r.ord_id JOIN cust_master c ON h.cust_id = c.cust_id ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: List the customer IDs of individuals who have both active platinum tier status ('P') and at least one support ticket categorized under billing ('BILL'). Show the customer ID, ordered by customer ID.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM cust_master WHERE tier_cd = 'P' INTERSECT SELECT cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE categ_cd = 'BILL' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: Find employee IDs of support staff who handled tickets categorized as technical ('TECH') but have never been assigned a ticket categorized as shipping ('SHIP'). Show the employee ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT assigned_emp_id FROM support_tkt WHERE categ_cd = 'TECH' AND assigned_emp_id IS NOT NULL EXCEPT SELECT assigned_emp_id FROM support_tkt WHERE categ_cd = 'SHIP' AND assigned_emp_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY assigned_emp_id ASC;

items.question: Retrieve the SKUs of products that appear in at least one order line with zero discount (disc_pct = 0.00) and also in at least one order line with a non-zero discount. Return the SKU, sorted ascending.
items.sql: SELECT sku FROM ord_line WHERE disc_pct = 0.00 INTERSECT SELECT sku FROM ord_line WHERE disc_pct > 0.00 ORDER BY sku ASC;

items.question: Which customer IDs have placed orders using the mobile app ('APP') and also placed orders using physical stores ('STR')? List the customer ID, sorted alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'APP' INTERSECT SELECT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'STR' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: Identify SKUs that have been ordered in quantity greater than 2 but have never experienced an inventory adjustment movement ('ADJ'). Return the SKU, ordered alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT sku FROM ord_line WHERE qty > 2 EXCEPT SELECT sku FROM inv_move WHERE mv_type = 'ADJ' ORDER BY sku ASC;

items.question: Find employee IDs who have approved at least one refund request and also have been assigned at least one support ticket. Show the employee ID, sorted ascending.
items.sql: SELECT approver_emp_id AS emp_id FROM refund_req WHERE approver_emp_id IS NOT NULL INTERSECT SELECT assigned_emp_id AS emp_id FROM support_tkt WHERE assigned_emp_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Which customer IDs opened a support ticket on or after '2026-04-01' but never had an order with status 'C' (cancelled)? Return the customer ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_status = 'C' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: List the customer IDs that belong to the North America sales region ('NA') and have a signup date before '2022-07-01'. Return the customer ID, ordered by customer ID.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM cust_master WHERE region_cd = 'NA' AND signup_dt < '2022-07-01' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: Find the distinct product SKUs that were ordered on '2026-04-03' and also ordered on '2026-04-04'. Return the SKU, ordered alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT l.sku FROM ord_line l JOIN ord_hdr h ON l.ord_id = h.ord_id WHERE h.ord_dt = '2026-04-03' INTERSECT SELECT l.sku FROM ord_line l JOIN ord_hdr h ON l.ord_id = h.ord_id WHERE h.ord_dt = '2026-04-04' ORDER BY sku ASC;

items.question: Get the warehouse IDs that hold inventory for SKU 'ELC-024' and also hold inventory for SKU 'ELC-025'. Show the warehouse ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT wh_id FROM inventory WHERE sku = 'ELC-024' INTERSECT SELECT wh_id FROM inventory WHERE sku = 'ELC-025' ORDER BY wh_id ASC;

items.question: Which employee IDs are listed as managers of other employees but do not belong to the management department ('MGT')? Show the manager employee ID, sorted ascending.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT mgr_emp_id FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NOT NULL EXCEPT SELECT emp_id FROM emp WHERE dept_cd = 'MGT' ORDER BY mgr_emp_id ASC;

items.question: Find customer IDs that placed orders in currency 'EUR' and also placed orders in currency 'GBP'. Return the customer ID, ordered alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE currency_cd = 'EUR' INTERSECT SELECT cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE currency_cd = 'GBP' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: List the employee IDs of support staff who logged a ticket event of type 'REPLY' but have never logged a ticket event of type 'ESCAL'. Return the employee ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT actor_emp_id FROM tkt_event WHERE evt_type = 'REPLY' AND actor_emp_id IS NOT NULL EXCEPT SELECT actor_emp_id FROM tkt_event WHERE evt_type = 'ESCAL' AND actor_emp_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY actor_emp_id ASC;

items.question: Which SKUs have positive on-hand quantity in warehouse 'W1' and also in warehouse 'W2'? Return the SKU, sorted ascending.
items.sql: SELECT sku FROM inventory WHERE wh_id = 'W1' AND on_hand_qty > 0 INTERSECT SELECT sku FROM inventory WHERE wh_id = 'W2' AND on_hand_qty > 0 ORDER BY sku ASC;

items.question: Identify customer IDs who raised support tickets through the phone channel ('PHN') and also through the web channel ('WEB'). Return the customer ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE channel_cd = 'PHN' INTERSECT SELECT cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: Find the product SKUs that have been included in an order with status 'D' (delivered) but have never been included in an order with status 'R' (returned). Show the SKU, ordered alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT l.sku FROM ord_line l JOIN ord_hdr h ON l.ord_id = h.ord_id WHERE h.ord_status = 'D' EXCEPT SELECT DISTINCT l.sku FROM ord_line l JOIN ord_hdr h ON l.ord_id = h.ord_id WHERE h.ord_status = 'R' ORDER BY sku ASC;

items.question: Which customer IDs have both standard tier status ('S') and active status (is_actv = 1)? Return the customer ID, sorted ascending.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM cust_master WHERE tier_cd = 'S' INTERSECT SELECT cust_id FROM cust_master WHERE is_actv = 1 ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: List employee IDs who have department code 'SUP' and were hired before '2020-01-01'. Return the employee ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id FROM emp WHERE dept_cd = 'SUP' INTERSECT SELECT emp_id FROM emp WHERE hire_dt < '2020-01-01' ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Find the SKUs of electronics products ('ELC') that have list price greater than 50.00 and have at least one inventory movement of type 'OUT'. Return the SKU, ordered alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT sku FROM prod_catalog WHERE categ_cd = 'ELC' AND list_prc > 50.00 INTERSECT SELECT sku FROM inv_move WHERE mv_type = 'OUT' ORDER BY sku ASC;

items.question: Which customer IDs have submitted refund requests with reason code 'DMG' (damaged) and also reason code 'LAT' (late delivery)? Return the customer ID, sorted alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT h.cust_id FROM refund_req r JOIN ord_hdr h ON r.ord_id = h.ord_id WHERE r.reason_cd = 'DMG' INTERSECT SELECT h.cust_id FROM refund_req r JOIN ord_hdr h ON r.ord_id = h.ord_id WHERE r.reason_cd = 'LAT' ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: List support ticket IDs that have experienced an event of type 'OPEN' and also an event of type 'CLOSE'. Return the ticket ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id FROM tkt_event WHERE evt_type = 'OPEN' INTERSECT SELECT tkt_id FROM tkt_event WHERE evt_type = 'CLOSE' ORDER BY tkt_id ASC;

items.question: Find the customer IDs of users who logged a web event of type 'CART' and also logged a web event of type 'PURCHASE'. Return the customer ID, ordered ascending.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id FROM web_event WHERE evt_type = 'CART' AND cust_id IS NOT NULL INTERSECT SELECT cust_id FROM web_event WHERE evt_type = 'PURCHASE' AND cust_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY cust_id ASC;

items.question: Which employee IDs appear as approvers in refund_req and also appear as assigned employees in support_tkt? Show the employee ID, sorted ascending.
items.sql: SELECT approver_emp_id AS emp_id FROM refund_req WHERE approver_emp_id IS NOT NULL INTERSECT SELECT assigned_emp_id AS emp_id FROM support_tkt WHERE assigned_emp_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Can you list the support ticket ID and customer ID for all tickets that were opened through the mobile app channel on 2026-04-03?
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE channel_cd = 'APP' AND opened_ts >= '2026-04-03 00:00:00' AND opened_ts <= '2026-04-03 23:59:59'

items.question: Show the order ID and order total amount for every order placed using the web channel that exceeds 500 USD.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' AND currency_cd = 'USD' AND ord_total_amt > 500.00

items.question: Give me the employee ID and employee name for staff members who belong to the support department.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE dept_cd = 'SUP'

items.question: What are the customer ID and customer name for clients in the North American region who belong to the platinum loyalty tier?
items.sql: SELECT cust_id, cust_nm FROM cust_master WHERE region_cd = 'NA' AND tier_cd = 'P'

items.question: Display the refund request ID and requested amount for all refund requests that are currently in pending status.
items.sql: SELECT rfd_id, rfd_amt FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'P'

items.question: Retrieve the ticket ID and opened timestamp for all critical severity support tickets.
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, opened_ts FROM support_tkt WHERE sev_lvl = 1

items.question: Which customers have never placed a single order in our system? Show their customer ID and customer name, ordered by customer name.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm FROM cust_master AS t1 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ord_hdr AS t2 WHERE t2.cust_id = t1.cust_id) ORDER BY t1.cust_nm, t1.cust_id

items.question: Show the refund request ID, order ID, and refund amount for requests where the refund amount is strictly greater than the approval threshold policy rule in force on 2025-12-01.
items.sql: SELECT t1.rfd_id, t1.ord_id, t1.rfd_amt FROM refund_req AS t1 WHERE t1.rfd_amt > CAST((SELECT t2.rule_val FROM policy_rule AS t2 WHERE t2.rule_key = 'refund_approval_threshold' AND '2025-12-01' BETWEEN t2.eff_from AND COALESCE(t2.eff_to, '9999-12-31')) AS DECIMAL(10,2))

items.question: List the customer ID and customer name for customers who have raised at least one support ticket categorized under billing.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN support_tkt AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t2.categ_cd = 'BILL'

items.question: Find all orders whose total amount is greater than the average order total amount for orders placed in the same currency during 2026. Show the order ID, currency code, and order total amount, ordered by order ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.ord_id, t1.currency_cd, t1.ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr AS t1 WHERE t1.ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND t1.ord_dt <= '2026-12-31' AND t1.ord_total_amt > (SELECT AVG(t2.ord_total_amt) FROM ord_hdr AS t2 WHERE t2.currency_cd = t1.currency_cd AND t2.ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND t2.ord_dt <= '2026-12-31') ORDER BY t1.ord_id

items.question: Give me the employee ID, employee name, and hire date for employees who were hired before their direct manager.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm, t1.hire_dt FROM emp AS t1 JOIN emp AS t2 ON t1.mgr_emp_id = t2.emp_id WHERE t1.hire_dt < t2.hire_dt

items.question: Which support tickets have never had an event recorded in the ticket history table? Return the ticket ID and opened timestamp, ordered by ticket ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t1.opened_ts FROM support_tkt AS t1 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM tkt_event AS t2 WHERE t2.tkt_id = t1.tkt_id) ORDER BY t1.tkt_id

items.question: Identify all orders that have multiple payment attempts recorded. Show the order ID and the count of payment attempts, ordered by payment count descending then order ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.ord_id, COUNT(*) AS pay_count FROM payment AS t1 GROUP BY t1.ord_id HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY pay_count DESC, t1.ord_id

items.question: Show the employee ID and employee name for employees who have approved at least one refund request where the request amount exceeded 150 USD, ordered by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm FROM emp AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.approver_emp_id WHERE t2.rfd_amt > 150.00 ORDER BY t1.emp_id

items.question: List the customer ID and customer name for customers who placed an order on 2026-04-03 and also had a support ticket opened on the exact same day.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id JOIN support_tkt AS t3 ON t1.cust_id = t3.cust_id WHERE t2.ord_dt = '2026-04-03' AND DATE(t3.opened_ts) = '2026-04-03'

items.question: For each support ticket, find its most recent event type and the timestamp of that event. Return the ticket ID, event type, and event timestamp for the latest event of each ticket, ordered by ticket ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t1.evt_type, t1.evt_ts FROM tkt_event AS t1 WHERE t1.evt_ts = (SELECT MAX(t2.evt_ts) FROM tkt_event AS t2 WHERE t2.tkt_id = t1.tkt_id) ORDER BY t1.tkt_id

items.question: Find all support tickets that were opened by customers who are currently marked as inactive (is_actv = 0). Return the ticket ID, customer ID, and opened timestamp, ordered by opened timestamp.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t1.cust_id, t1.opened_ts FROM support_tkt AS t1 JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t2.is_actv = 0 ORDER BY t1.opened_ts, t1.tkt_id

items.question: Show the customer ID and customer name for customers whose total spending across all their orders is strictly greater than the overall average order total across all customers in the database, ordered by customer ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id GROUP BY t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm HAVING SUM(t2.ord_total_amt) > (SELECT AVG(t3.ord_total_amt) FROM ord_hdr AS t3) ORDER BY t1.cust_id

items.question: Which employees have handled support tickets across more than two distinct channels? Return the employee ID, employee name, and the count of distinct channels, ordered by channel count descending then employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm, COUNT(DISTINCT t2.channel_cd) AS channel_cnt FROM emp AS t1 JOIN support_tkt AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.assigned_emp_id GROUP BY t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t2.channel_cd) > 2 ORDER BY channel_cnt DESC, t1.emp_id

items.question: List the refund request ID, order ID, and refund amount for any refund request where the requested amount is higher than the maximum order total amount placed by that same customer. Order by refund request ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.rfd_id, t1.ord_id, t1.rfd_amt FROM refund_req AS t1 JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id WHERE t1.rfd_amt > (SELECT MAX(t3.ord_total_amt) FROM ord_hdr AS t3 WHERE t3.cust_id = t2.cust_id) ORDER BY t1.rfd_id

items.question: Find the order ID, customer ID, and order total amount for orders that have a refund request whose amount is greater than 50% of the order's total amount. Order by order ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.ord_id, t1.cust_id, t1.ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id WHERE t2.rfd_amt > (t1.ord_total_amt * 0.50) ORDER BY t1.ord_id

items.question: Identify employees who have approved refund requests, but have never been assigned a single support ticket. Return their employee ID and employee name, ordered by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm FROM emp AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.approver_emp_id WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM support_tkt AS t3 WHERE t3.assigned_emp_id = t1.emp_id) ORDER BY t1.emp_id

items.question: Show the employee ID and employee name for staff members who have approved refund requests totaling more than 300 USD in aggregate. Order by total approved amount descending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm, SUM(t2.rfd_amt) AS total_approved FROM emp AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.approver_emp_id WHERE t2.status_cd = 'A' GROUP BY t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm HAVING SUM(t2.rfd_amt) > 300.00 ORDER BY total_approved DESC, t1.emp_id

items.question: Find support tickets that took longer to close than the severity 1 SLA hours policy rule in force when the ticket was opened. Return the ticket ID, opened timestamp, and closed timestamp for these tickets, ordered by ticket ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t1.opened_ts, t1.closed_ts FROM support_tkt AS t1 WHERE t1.closed_ts IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(HOUR, t1.opened_ts, t1.closed_ts) > CAST((SELECT t2.rule_val FROM policy_rule AS t2 WHERE t2.rule_key = 'sla_hours_sev1' AND DATE(t1.opened_ts) BETWEEN t2.eff_from AND COALESCE(t2.eff_to, '9999-12-31')) AS UNSIGNED) ORDER BY t1.tkt_id

items.question: Can you show me the total number of support tickets and how many of those were high severity (sev_lvl 2) for each category code in April 2026?
items.sql: SELECT t1.categ_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_tickets, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.sev_lvl = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_sev_count FROM support_tkt AS t1 WHERE t1.opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND t1.opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY t1.categ_cd

items.question: Break down support tickets opened in April 2026 by their channel code, showing the total ticket count alongside the count of critical severity (sev_lvl 1) tickets.
items.sql: SELECT t1.channel_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_tickets, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.sev_lvl = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS critical_count FROM support_tkt AS t1 WHERE t1.opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND t1.opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY t1.channel_cd

items.question: For each channel code in April 2026, list the total number of support tickets, and separately count how many are currently closed versus still open (where closed_ts is null).
items.sql: SELECT t1.channel_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_tickets, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.closed_ts IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS closed_count, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.closed_ts IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS open_count FROM support_tkt AS t1 WHERE t1.opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND t1.opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY t1.channel_cd

items.question: Show the count of refund requests by their status code for requests made in the year 2025, displaying approved, denied, and pending counts side by side.
items.sql: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN status_cd = 'A' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS approved_count, SUM(CASE WHEN status_cd = 'D' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS denied_count, SUM(CASE WHEN status_cd = 'P' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS pending_count FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt <= '2025-12-31'

items.question: For each reason code in the refund requests made during 2025, show the total number of requests and the total sum of requested refund amounts.
items.sql: SELECT reason_cd, COUNT(*) AS request_count, SUM(rfd_amt) AS total_amount FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY reason_cd

items.question: Provide a summary of refund requests in 2025 grouped by reason code, showing the total count of requests, the sum of approved amounts, and the sum of denied amounts.
items.sql: SELECT reason_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_requests, SUM(CASE WHEN status_cd = 'A' THEN rfd_amt ELSE 0 END) AS approved_amt, SUM(CASE WHEN status_cd = 'D' THEN rfd_amt ELSE 0 END) AS denied_amt FROM refund_req WHERE req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND req_dt <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY reason_cd

items.question: For each loyalty tier code in the customer master, list the total number of customers and the count of active customers (is_actv = 1).
items.sql: SELECT tier_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN is_actv = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_customers FROM cust_master GROUP BY tier_cd

items.question: Summarize customers by region code, giving the total customer count, active customer count, and inactive customer count side by side.
items.sql: SELECT region_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_customers, SUM(CASE WHEN is_actv = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_count, SUM(CASE WHEN is_actv = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS inactive_count FROM cust_master GROUP BY region_cd

items.question: For every sales region code, calculate the active customer percentage by dividing active customers by total customers, alongside the raw counts for 2022 signups.
items.sql: SELECT region_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_signups, SUM(CASE WHEN is_actv = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS active_signups, (SUM(CASE WHEN is_actv = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(*) AS active_pct FROM cust_master WHERE signup_dt >= '2022-01-01' AND signup_dt <= '2022-12-31' GROUP BY region_cd

items.question: Show the order count and total order amount for each channel code for orders placed in the first half of 2026 (between 2026-01-01 and 2026-06-30).
items.sql: SELECT channel_cd, COUNT(*) AS order_count, SUM(ord_total_amt) AS total_revenue FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt <= '2026-06-30' GROUP BY channel_cd

items.question: For orders placed in 2026, break down totals by order status code, showing the count of orders and sum of order amounts for delivered (D) and cancelled (C) statuses separately.
items.sql: SELECT ord_status, COUNT(*) AS ord_count, SUM(ord_total_amt) AS total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt <= '2026-12-31' GROUP BY ord_status

items.question: Analyze 2026 orders by channel code, showing total orders, sum of amounts, and specific counts for shipped (S) versus delivered (D) order statuses.
items.sql: SELECT channel_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_orders, SUM(ord_total_amt) AS total_amount, SUM(CASE WHEN ord_status = 'S' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shipped_count, SUM(CASE WHEN ord_status = 'D' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delivered_count FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt <= '2026-12-31' GROUP BY channel_cd

items.question: For each employee department code, count the total number of employees and show how many report to someone versus having a null manager.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_employees, SUM(CASE WHEN mgr_emp_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS with_manager, SUM(CASE WHEN mgr_emp_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS top_level FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd

items.question: Give me a breakdown of employees hired each year from 2018 through 2021, showing total hires and the count of employees in the SUP department.
items.sql: SELECT LEFT(hire_dt, 4) AS hire_year, COUNT(*) AS total_hires, SUM(CASE WHEN dept_cd = 'SUP' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sup_hires FROM emp WHERE hire_dt >= '2018-01-01' AND hire_dt <= '2021-12-31' GROUP BY LEFT(hire_dt, 4)

items.question: For each department code, compute the total number of employees and the percentage of staff belonging to the MGT or FIN departments.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, COUNT(*) AS dept_count, (SUM(CASE WHEN dept_cd IN ('MGT', 'FIN') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / COUNT(*) AS leadership_fin_pct FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd

items.question: Show the count of payment attempts by payment method code for 2025, detailing settled payments versus failed or refunded attempts side by side.
items.sql: SELECT method_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_attempts, SUM(CASE WHEN pay_status = 'S' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS settled_count, SUM(CASE WHEN pay_status IN ('F', 'R') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_or_refunded FROM payment WHERE paid_ts >= '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND paid_ts <= '2025-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY method_cd

items.question: For payment attempts in 2025, calculate the total payment amount grouped by method code and currency code, separating settled amounts from failed amounts.
items.sql: SELECT method_cd, currency_cd, SUM(pay_amt) AS total_amount, SUM(CASE WHEN pay_status = 'S' THEN pay_amt ELSE 0 END) AS settled_amount, SUM(CASE WHEN pay_status = 'F' THEN pay_amt ELSE 0 END) AS failed_amount FROM payment WHERE paid_ts >= '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND paid_ts <= '2025-12-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY method_cd, currency_cd

items.question: For each warehouse region code, list the total number of warehouses and count how many have 'Hub' in their name.
items.sql: SELECT region_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_warehouses, SUM(CASE WHEN wh_nm LIKE '%Hub%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS hub_count FROM warehouse GROUP BY region_cd

items.question: For each stock movement type (mv_type), count how many movements occurred and sum the quantity moved for movements recorded in October 2025.
items.sql: SELECT mv_type, COUNT(*) AS movement_count, SUM(qty) AS total_qty_moved FROM inv_move WHERE mv_ts >= '2025-10-01 00:00:00' AND mv_ts <= '2025-10-31 23:59:59' GROUP BY mv_type

items.question: Analyze web clickstream events in November 2025 by event type, showing total event counts and the number of distinct customer sessions involved.
items.sql: SELECT evt_type, COUNT(*) AS total_events, COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) AS unique_sessions FROM web_event WHERE evt_ts >= '2025-11-01 00:00:00' AND evt_ts <= '2025-11-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY evt_type

items.question: For each product category code in the product catalog, show the total product count and the number of discontinued products (disc_flag = 1).
items.sql: SELECT categ_cd, COUNT(*) AS total_products, SUM(CASE WHEN disc_flag = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS discontinued_count FROM prod_catalog GROUP BY categ_cd

items.question: For support tickets opened in April 2026, join with customer master to show ticket counts grouped by customer tier code, separating critical (sev_lvl 1) from non-critical tickets.
items.sql: SELECT t2.tier_cd, COUNT(*) AS ticket_count, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.sev_lvl = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS critical_count, SUM(CASE WHEN t1.sev_lvl > 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS non_critical_count FROM support_tkt AS t1 INNER JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND t1.opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' GROUP BY t2.tier_cd

items.question: For orders placed in 2026, join with customer master to evaluate revenue by customer region code, comparing total sales from platinum (P) tier customers against gold (G) tier customers.
items.sql: SELECT t2.region_cd, SUM(t1.ord_total_amt) AS total_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN t2.tier_cd = 'P' THEN t1.ord_total_amt ELSE 0 END) AS platinum_revenue, SUM(CASE WHEN t2.tier_cd = 'G' THEN t1.ord_total_amt ELSE 0 END) AS gold_revenue FROM ord_hdr AS t1 INNER JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND t1.ord_dt <= '2026-12-31' GROUP BY t2.region_cd

items.question: For refund requests in 2025, join with order headers to compare refund amounts across different sales channels, showing total refund count, total requested amount, and the share of refunds coming from WEB channels.
items.sql: SELECT t2.channel_cd, COUNT(*) AS refund_count, SUM(t1.rfd_amt) AS total_rfd_amt, SUM(CASE WHEN t2.channel_cd = 'WEB' THEN t1.rfd_amt ELSE 0 END) AS web_rfd_amt, (SUM(CASE WHEN t2.channel_cd = 'WEB' THEN t1.rfd_amt ELSE 0 END) * 100.0) / SUM(t1.rfd_amt) AS web_rfd_share FROM refund_req AS t1 INNER JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id WHERE t1.req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND t1.req_dt <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY t2.channel_cd

items.question: A pending refund request is one where the status code is P. Show the refund request ID and the amount requested for all pending refund requests where the amount is greater than 100.00, ordered by amount descending.
items.sql: SELECT rfd_id, rfd_amt FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'P' AND rfd_amt > 100.00 ORDER BY rfd_amt DESC, rfd_id ASC

items.question: A platinum customer is one whose tier code is P and whose record is active (is_actv equals 1). List the customer ID and customer name for all platinum active customers, ordered by customer name ascending.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id, cust_nm FROM cust_master WHERE tier_cd = 'P' AND is_actv = 1 ORDER BY cust_nm ASC, cust_id ASC

items.question: A critical support ticket is one with a severity level of 1. Show the ticket ID and customer ID for all open critical tickets (closed timestamp is null), ordered by opened timestamp ascending, breaking ties by ticket ID.
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE sev_lvl = 1 AND closed_ts IS NULL ORDER BY opened_ts ASC, tkt_id ASC

items.question: A cancelled order is one where the order status code is C. Retrieve the order ID and customer ID for orders placed in the WEB channel with status C, ordered by order date ascending.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, cust_id FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' AND ord_status = 'C' ORDER BY ord_dt ASC, ord_id ASC

items.question: An active customer is one with is_actv equal to 1. Show the region code and the count of active customers in each region, ordered by region code ascending.
items.sql: SELECT region_cd, COUNT(*) FROM cust_master WHERE is_actv = 1 GROUP BY region_cd ORDER BY region_cd ASC

items.question: A returned order has an order status code of R. Report the order ID and order total amount for returned orders in USD currency, sorted by order total descending, then order ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_status = 'R' AND currency_cd = 'USD' ORDER BY ord_total_amt DESC, ord_id ASC

items.question: A phone order has channel code PHN. Find the order ID, customer ID, and order total amount for phone orders placed on or after 2026-07-01, ordered by order date descending, then order ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, cust_id, ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'PHN' AND ord_dt >= '2026-07-01' ORDER BY ord_dt DESC, ord_id ASC

items.question: A resolved support ticket is one that has a non-null closed timestamp. For each support department employee (dept_cd is SUP), count how many tickets they were assigned to that were closed, showing the employee ID and the count, ordered by the count descending, then employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.assigned_emp_id, COUNT(*) FROM support_tkt AS t1 JOIN emp AS t2 ON t1.assigned_emp_id = t2.emp_id WHERE t2.dept_cd = 'SUP' AND t1.closed_ts IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t1.assigned_emp_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, t1.assigned_emp_id ASC

items.question: A high-severity ticket is one with severity level 2. Show the ticket ID, customer name, and opened timestamp for high-severity tickets opened between 2026-04-01 and 2026-04-30, ordered by opened timestamp ascending, then ticket ID.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t2.cust_nm, t1.opened_ts FROM support_tkt AS t1 JOIN cust_master AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.sev_lvl = 2 AND t1.opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND t1.opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59' ORDER BY t1.opened_ts ASC, t1.tkt_id ASC

items.question: An approved refund is one where the status code is A. Find the employee ID, employee name, and the count of approved refund requests they decided on, for employees who approved more than 0 requests, ordered by the count descending, then employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm, COUNT(t2.rfd_id) FROM emp AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.approver_emp_id WHERE t2.status_cd = 'A' GROUP BY t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm ORDER BY COUNT(t2.rfd_id) DESC, t1.emp_id ASC

items.question: A damaged refund request has reason code DMG. List the order ID, refund amount, and requested date for refund requests due to damage where the amount exceeded 90.00, sorted by requested date ascending, then refund ID.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, rfd_amt, req_dt FROM refund_req WHERE reason_cd = 'DMG' AND rfd_amt > 90.00 ORDER BY req_dt ASC, rfd_id ASC

items.question: A duplicate charge refund request has reason code DUP. Show the customer ID, order ID, and refund amount for duplicate charge refund requests requested in 2025, ordered by refund amount descending, then order ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_id, t2.ord_id, t2.rfd_amt FROM ord_hdr AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.ord_id = t2.ord_id WHERE t2.reason_cd = 'DUP' AND t2.req_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND t2.req_dt <= '2025-12-31' ORDER BY t2.rfd_amt DESC, t2.ord_id ASC

items.question: A billing support ticket has category code BILL. Show the customer name, support ticket ID, and opened timestamp for billing tickets raised by platinum customers (tier code P), ordered by opened timestamp ascending, then ticket ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_nm, t2.tkt_id, t2.opened_ts FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN support_tkt AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.tier_cd = 'P' AND t2.categ_cd = 'BILL' ORDER BY t2.opened_ts ASC, t2.tkt_id ASC

items.question: An escalated support ticket event has event type ESCAL. Find the support ticket ID, customer ID, and the count of escalation events for each ticket that has at least one escalation event, ordered by the count descending, then ticket ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t1.cust_id, COUNT(t2.evt_id) FROM support_tkt AS t1 JOIN tkt_event AS t2 ON t1.tkt_id = t2.tkt_id WHERE t2.evt_type = 'ESCAL' GROUP BY t1.tkt_id, t1.cust_id ORDER BY COUNT(t2.evt_id) DESC, t1.tkt_id ASC

items.question: A high-value order is one where the order total amount exceeds 500.00. For each customer in the NA region, count how many high-value orders they placed, showing the customer ID, customer name, and the order count, ordered by the order count descending, then customer ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm, COUNT(t2.ord_id) FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.region_cd = 'NA' AND t2.ord_total_amt > 500.00 GROUP BY t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm ORDER BY COUNT(t2.ord_id) DESC, t1.cust_id ASC

items.question: A closed support ticket is one with a non-null closed timestamp. Calculate the average resolution time in hours for closed tickets in each category code, showing the category code and the average hours (computed as the difference between closed timestamp and opened timestamp), ordered by the average hours ascending.
items.sql: SELECT categ_cd, AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(HOUR, opened_ts, closed_ts)) FROM support_tkt WHERE closed_ts IS NOT NULL GROUP BY categ_cd ORDER BY AVG(TIMESTAMPDIFF(HOUR, opened_ts, closed_ts)) ASC

items.question: A manager-approved refund threshold is defined by the policy rule where rule key is 'refund_approval_threshold' and effective on 2026-04-01. List the refund request ID, order ID, and refund amount for refund requests whose amount is greater than that threshold, ordered by refund amount descending, then refund ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.rfd_id, t1.ord_id, t1.rfd_amt FROM refund_req AS t1 JOIN policy_rule AS t2 ON t2.rule_key = 'refund_approval_threshold' AND t1.req_dt >= t2.eff_from AND (t2.eff_to IS NULL OR t1.req_dt <= t2.eff_to) WHERE t1.rfd_amt > CAST(t2.rule_val AS DECIMAL(10,2)) ORDER BY t1.rfd_amt DESC, t1.rfd_id ASC

items.question: An active customer has is_actv equal to 1. For each sales region, calculate the total order amount across all orders placed by active customers, showing the region code and the total order amount, ordered by the total order amount descending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.region_cd, SUM(t2.ord_total_amt) FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN ord_hdr AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t1.is_actv = 1 GROUP BY t1.region_cd ORDER BY SUM(t2.ord_total_amt) DESC

items.question: A replied ticket event has event type REPLY. Find the employee ID, employee name, and the total count of reply events performed by each support department employee (dept_cd is SUP), ordered by the reply count descending, then employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm, COUNT(t2.evt_id) FROM emp AS t1 JOIN tkt_event AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.actor_emp_id WHERE t1.dept_cd = 'SUP' AND t2.evt_type = 'REPLY' GROUP BY t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm ORDER BY COUNT(t2.evt_id) DESC, t1.emp_id ASC

items.question: A delayed policy rule is represented by rule key 'sla_hours_sev1' active on 2026-04-01. Show the ticket ID, customer ID, and opened timestamp for critical severity tickets (sev_lvl equals 1) opened on 2026-04-01 where the time from opening to closing exceeded the hours specified in that policy rule, ordered by opened timestamp ascending, then ticket ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.tkt_id, t1.cust_id, t1.opened_ts FROM support_tkt AS t1 JOIN policy_rule AS t2 ON t2.rule_key = 'sla_hours_sev1' AND t1.opened_ts >= t2.eff_from AND (t2.eff_to IS NULL OR t1.opened_ts <= CONCAT(t2.eff_to, ' 23:59:59')) WHERE t1.sev_lvl = 1 AND t1.closed_ts IS NOT NULL AND TIMESTAMPDIFF(HOUR, t1.opened_ts, t1.closed_ts) > CAST(t2.rule_val AS UNSIGNED) ORDER BY t1.opened_ts ASC, t1.tkt_id ASC

items.question: A denied refund has status code D. For each employee who decided on refunds, count how many requests they denied, showing the employee ID, employee name, and the count of denied requests, ordered by the count descending, then employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm, COUNT(t2.rfd_id) FROM emp AS t1 JOIN refund_req AS t2 ON t1.emp_id = t2.approver_emp_id WHERE t2.status_cd = 'D' GROUP BY t1.emp_id, t1.emp_nm ORDER BY COUNT(t2.rfd_id) DESC, t1.emp_id ASC

items.question: A web channel support ticket has channel code WEB. Find the customer name and the count of web support tickets for each customer who has raised more than 1 web support ticket, ordered by the ticket count descending, then customer name ascending.
items.sql: SELECT t1.cust_nm, COUNT(t2.tkt_id) FROM cust_master AS t1 JOIN support_tkt AS t2 ON t1.cust_id = t2.cust_id WHERE t2.channel_cd = 'WEB' GROUP BY t1.cust_id, t1.cust_nm HAVING COUNT(t2.tkt_id) > 1 ORDER BY COUNT(t2.tkt_id) DESC, t1.cust_nm ASC

items.question: A standard tier customer has tier code S. Report the customer ID, customer name, and signup date for standard tier customers who signed up in the year 2022, ordered by signup date ascending, then customer ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT cust_id, cust_nm, signup_dt FROM cust_master WHERE tier_cd = 'S' AND signup_dt >= '2022-01-01' AND signup_dt <= '2022-12-31' ORDER BY signup_dt ASC, cust_id ASC

items.question: A delivered order has order status code D. Show the order ID, order date, and order total amount for delivered orders placed via the application channel (APP) in the EUR currency, ordered by order date ascending, then order ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, ord_dt, ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_status = 'D' AND channel_cd = 'APP' AND currency_cd = 'EUR' ORDER BY ord_dt ASC, ord_id ASC

items.question: Can you list the employee ID and full name for Amara Singh's direct reports, ordered by employee ID ascending?
items.sql: SELECT e1.emp_id, e1.emp_nm FROM emp e1 JOIN emp e2 ON e1.mgr_emp_id = e2.emp_id WHERE e2.emp_nm = 'Amara Singh' ORDER BY e1.emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the employee ID and full name of everyone who reports directly to employee E-001, sorted by name alphabetically.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id = 'E-001' ORDER BY emp_nm ASC;

items.question: What are the employee IDs and names of the managers who have direct reports in department SUP? Show them sorted by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.emp_id, m.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.mgr_emp_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.dept_cd = 'SUP' ORDER BY m.emp_id ASC;

items.question: List the employee ID, name, and department code for all staff members who do not have any direct reports, sorted by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, dept_cd FROM emp WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT mgr_emp_id FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Retrieve the department code and the total count of employees in each department, ordered by the headcount descending, then department code ascending.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, COUNT(*) AS emp_count FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd ORDER BY emp_count DESC, dept_cd ASC;

items.question: Find the employee ID and name of the direct manager of employee E-003.
items.sql: SELECT m.emp_id, m.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.mgr_emp_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.emp_id = 'E-003';

items.question: Using a recursive CTE, list all employee IDs and names in the reporting chain under employee E-001, including E-001, ordered by employee ID.
items.sql: WITH RECURSIVE report_chain AS (SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, mgr_emp_id FROM emp WHERE emp_id = 'E-001' UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm, e.mgr_emp_id FROM emp e JOIN report_chain r ON e.mgr_emp_id = r.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM report_chain ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the employee ID and name of all employees who belong to the same department as their direct manager, sorted by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.mgr_emp_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.dept_cd = m.dept_cd ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;

items.question: List the department code and the number of managers (employees who have at least one direct report) in each department, sorted by department code.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, COUNT(DISTINCT m.emp_id) AS manager_count FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.emp_id = m.mgr_emp_id GROUP BY dept_cd ORDER BY dept_cd ASC;

items.question: Give me the employee ID and name for employees hired before 2020-01-01 who are themselves managers of other staff, ordered by hire date.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.emp_id = m.mgr_emp_id WHERE e.hire_dt < '2020-01-01' ORDER BY e.hire_dt ASC, e.emp_id ASC;

items.question: List the employee ID and name of employees who report to E-002 and also have direct reports of their own, ordered by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e1.emp_id, e1.emp_nm FROM emp e1 JOIN emp e2 ON e1.emp_id = e2.mgr_emp_id WHERE e1.mgr_emp_id = 'E-002' ORDER BY e1.emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the top-level managers (employees with no manager) along with the count of their direct reports, sorted by direct report count descending.
items.sql: SELECT m.emp_id, m.emp_nm, COUNT(e.emp_id) AS direct_count FROM emp m LEFT JOIN emp e ON e.mgr_emp_id = m.emp_id WHERE m.mgr_emp_id IS NULL GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.emp_nm ORDER BY direct_count DESC, m.emp_id ASC;

items.question: Using recursion, find the full reporting hierarchy depth (levels from top manager E-001) for all employees under E-001, returning employee ID, name, and level, ordered by level then employee ID.
items.sql: WITH RECURSIVE hierarchy AS (SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, mgr_emp_id, 1 AS lvl FROM emp WHERE emp_id = 'E-001' UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm, e.mgr_emp_id, h.lvl + 1 FROM emp e JOIN hierarchy h ON e.mgr_emp_id = h.emp_id) SELECT emp_id, emp_nm, lvl FROM hierarchy ORDER BY lvl ASC, emp_id ASC;

items.question: List the department code and the total number of support tickets assigned to employees in each department, ordered by ticket count descending.
items.sql: SELECT e.dept_cd, COUNT(t.tkt_id) AS tkt_count FROM emp e JOIN support_tkt t ON e.emp_id = t.assigned_emp_id GROUP BY e.dept_cd ORDER BY tkt_count DESC, e.dept_cd ASC;

items.question: Show the employee ID and name of employees in department FIN who have approved at least one refund request, sorted by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN refund_req r ON e.emp_id = r.approver_emp_id WHERE e.dept_cd = 'FIN' ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;

items.question: What are the employee ID and name of staff members who have both handled support ticket events and approved refund requests? Sort by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN tkt_event te ON e.emp_id = te.actor_emp_id JOIN refund_req r ON e.emp_id = r.approver_emp_id ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;

items.question: List the manager employee ID and the count of unique departments managed by their direct reports, ordered by manager ID.
items.sql: SELECT m.emp_id AS mgr_emp_id, COUNT(DISTINCT e.dept_cd) AS dept_count FROM emp m JOIN emp e ON m.emp_id = e.mgr_emp_id GROUP BY m.emp_id ORDER BY m.emp_id ASC;

items.question: Display the employee ID and name of employees who were hired in 2019 and report to a manager in the MGT department, ordered by hire date.
items.sql: SELECT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN emp m ON e.mgr_emp_id = m.emp_id WHERE e.hire_dt >= '2019-01-01' AND e.hire_dt < '2020-01-01' AND m.dept_cd = 'MGT' ORDER BY e.hire_dt ASC;

items.question: Find the employee ID and name of employees who have never been assigned any support tickets, sorted by employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE emp_id NOT IN (SELECT DISTINCT assigned_emp_id FROM support_tkt WHERE assigned_emp_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: Using a recursive CTE, count how many total descendants (subordinates at any level) employee E-001 has, returning just the count.
items.sql: WITH RECURSIVE sub_tree AS (SELECT emp_id FROM emp WHERE mgr_emp_id = 'E-001' UNION ALL SELECT e.emp_id FROM emp e JOIN sub_tree st ON e.mgr_emp_id = st.emp_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_descendants FROM sub_tree;

items.question: List each department code and the earliest hire date among employees in that department, sorted by department code.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, MIN(hire_dt) AS earliest_hire FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd ORDER BY dept_cd ASC;

items.question: Show the employee ID and name of employees who approved refund requests where the refund amount exceeded 100.00, sorted by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT DISTINCT e.emp_id, e.emp_nm FROM emp e JOIN refund_req r ON e.emp_id = r.approver_emp_id WHERE r.rfd_amt > 100.00 ORDER BY e.emp_id ASC;

items.question: Retrieve the department code and the average tenure (expressed as years from hire date to 2026-10-31) for employees in each department, ordered by department code.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, AVG(DATEDIFF('2026-10-31', hire_dt) / 365.25) AS avg_tenure_years FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd ORDER BY dept_cd ASC;

items.question: List the employee ID and name of employees who are managers and have at least 2 direct reports, ordered by employee ID.
items.sql: SELECT m.emp_id, m.emp_nm FROM emp m JOIN emp e ON m.emp_id = e.mgr_emp_id GROUP BY m.emp_id, m.emp_nm HAVING COUNT(e.emp_id) >= 2 ORDER BY m.emp_id ASC;

items.question: Can you list the total refund amount grouped by the refund reason code for all requests decided during 2025? Show the reason code and the total requested amount, ordered by the total amount descending, then by the reason code ascending.
items.sql: SELECT reason_cd, SUM(rfd_amt) FROM refund_req WHERE decided_dt >= '2025-01-01' AND decided_dt <= '2025-12-31' GROUP BY reason_cd ORDER BY SUM(rfd_amt) DESC, reason_cd ASC;

items.question: How many support tickets were opened via the mobile app channel in April 2026? Give me just the count.
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM support_tkt WHERE channel_cd = 'APP' AND opened_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND opened_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59';

items.question: Find the full name and employee ID of every support department employee hired before 2020. Show the employee ID and full name, ordered by hire date ascending, then by employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE dept_cd = 'SUP' AND hire_dt < '2020-01-01' ORDER BY hire_dt ASC, emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the count of platinum tier customers located in the North America region who signed up since July 1st, 2022.
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cust_master WHERE tier_cd = 'P' AND region_cd = 'NA' AND signup_dt >= '2022-07-01';

items.question: What is the average order total amount for orders placed through the web channel in the Euro currency during the first half of 2026? Return just the average amount.
items.sql: SELECT AVG(ord_total_amt) FROM ord_hdr WHERE channel_cd = 'WEB' AND currency_cd = 'EUR' AND ord_dt >= '2026-01-01' AND ord_dt <= '2026-06-30';

items.question: List all pending refund requests where the requested amount exceeds 100 USD equivalent. Show the refund request ID, order ID, and requested amount, ordered by requested amount descending, then by refund request ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT rfd_id, ord_id, rfd_amt FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'P' AND rfd_amt > 100.00 ORDER BY rfd_amt DESC, rfd_id ASC;

items.question: For each sales region, how many active customers do we have who are in the standard loyalty tier? Show the region code and the customer count, sorted by customer count descending, then region code ascending.
items.sql: SELECT region_cd, COUNT(*) FROM cust_master WHERE tier_cd = 'S' AND is_actv = 1 GROUP BY region_cd ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, region_cd ASC;

items.question: Which employees approved refund requests with the reason code for damaged goods? Show the employee ID and the count of approved requests, ordered by the count descending, then employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT approver_emp_id, COUNT(*) FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'A' AND reason_cd = 'DMG' AND approver_emp_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY approver_emp_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, approver_emp_id ASC;

items.question: Show the total number of support tickets opened in each category where the severity level is critical. Display the category code and ticket count, ordered by ticket count descending, then category code ascending.
items.sql: SELECT categ_cd, COUNT(*) FROM support_tkt WHERE sev_lvl = 1 GROUP BY categ_cd ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, categ_cd ASC;

items.question: Give me the count of orders that have a cancelled status and were placed using the phone channel.
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_status = 'C' AND channel_cd = 'PHN';

items.question: List the full names of employees in the finance department who report directly to manager E-006. Show their employee ID and full name, ordered by employee ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT emp_id, emp_nm FROM emp WHERE dept_cd = 'FIN' AND mgr_emp_id = 'E-006' ORDER BY emp_id ASC;

items.question: What was the policy value for the refund approval threshold rule in force on January 15th, 2026? Return just the rule value.
items.sql: SELECT rule_val FROM policy_rule WHERE rule_key = 'refund_approval_threshold' AND eff_from <= '2026-01-15' AND (eff_to >= '2026-01-15' OR eff_to IS NULL);

items.question: Count how many ticket history events of type 'CLOSE' were performed by employee E-010 during April 2026.
items.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tkt_event WHERE evt_type = 'CLOSE' AND actor_emp_id = 'E-010' AND evt_ts >= '2026-04-01 00:00:00' AND evt_ts <= '2026-04-30 23:59:59';

items.question: Find all support tickets in the billing category that are still open, meaning their closed timestamp is null. Show the ticket ID, customer ID, and opened timestamp, ordered by opened timestamp ascending, then ticket ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, cust_id, opened_ts FROM support_tkt WHERE categ_cd = 'BILL' AND closed_ts IS NULL ORDER BY opened_ts ASC, tkt_id ASC;

items.question: What is the maximum refund amount requested for orders where the reason code was due to a duplicate charge? Return the max amount.

items.question: Show the number of customers in each loyalty tier for the Asia Pacific sales region. Display the tier code and the count, ordered by the count descending, then tier code ascending.

items.question: List the order IDs and their total amounts for all orders placed in July 2026 that have a delivered status. Sort by order total amount descending, then order ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT ord_id, ord_total_amt FROM ord_hdr WHERE ord_status = 'D' AND ord_dt >= '2026-07-01' AND ord_dt <= '2026-07-31' ORDER BY ord_total_amt DESC, ord_id ASC;

items.question: How many support tickets have a severity level of 3 and arrived through the store channel?

items.question: Find all refund requests that were denied and had an amount greater than 150. Show the refund request ID, order ID, and requested amount, ordered by requested amount descending, then refund ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT rfd_id, ord_id, rfd_amt FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'D' AND rfd_amt > 150.00 ORDER BY rfd_amt DESC, rfd_id ASC;

items.question: Show the count of employees in each department code. Display the department code and employee count, ordered by employee count descending, then department code ascending.
items.sql: SELECT dept_cd, COUNT(*) FROM emp GROUP BY dept_cd ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, dept_cd ASC;

items.question: Which employee approved the highest number of refund requests? Show the employee ID and the count of approved requests, ordered by the count descending, then employee ID ascending, and limit to the top 1.
items.sql: SELECT approver_emp_id, COUNT(*) FROM refund_req WHERE status_cd = 'A' AND approver_emp_id IS NOT NULL GROUP BY approver_emp_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, approver_emp_id ASC LIMIT 1;

items.question: Retrieve the ticket IDs and customer IDs for all support tickets categorized under shipping that were opened after April 5th, 2026. Order by opened timestamp ascending, then ticket ID ascending.
items.sql: SELECT tkt_id, cust_id FROM support_tkt WHERE categ_cd = 'SHIP' AND opened_ts > '2026-04-05 23:59:59' ORDER BY opened_ts ASC, tkt_id ASC;

items.question: Count the total number of inactive customers across all regions who are in the gold tier.

items.question: Show me the financial totals for Q1.
items.reply: -- CLARIFY: Are you looking for order revenue, refund amounts, employee salaries, or payment totals for Q1?

items.question: Which employee handled the most cases?
items.reply: -- CLARIFY: Are you measuring workload by support tickets assigned, ticket events performed, or refund requests approved?

items.question: What is the refund rate?
items.reply: -- CLARIFY: Do you mean the ratio of refund request counts to total orders, or the sum of refund amounts compared to total order revenue?

items.question: How many escalations happened?
